expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: type Subscription = TrialingSub | ActiveSub | PastDueSub | CanceledSub; with status: "trialing" etc. as literal discriminants

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: CanceledSub has only cancelReason/voluntary; TrialingSub only trialEndDate — "Accessing `trialEndDate` on canceled | Narrowing — field doesn't exist on that variant"

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: function assertNever(x: never): never { ... } used as `default: return assertNever(sub);`

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: SubscriptionBase uses `id: string; customerId: string; planId: string;` — no branded/nominal types; cancelReason is also bare string

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: No transition function; response says "Business logic errors ... aren't prevented by this shape — those need domain methods or state machine transitions" but does not provide one

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: "## What this makes impossible (Control rung)" table mapping each misuse to its device

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: "Bag of optionals permits nonsense" listed as the hazard; primary recommendation is the union
